The paper evaluates MLLMs on generating answers to visual questions and reasoning about vision-knowledge conflicts, including open-ended, multiple-choice, and yes-no responses.

To label the correctness of MLLMs responses for the open-ended questions, we design our evaluation criteria... The annotators are asked to determine the correctness of MLLMs' responses based on two criteria: Relevancy (0 or 1) and Responsiveness (0 or 1).

For Open-Ended questions, due to the complexity of the task (i.e., evaluating both textual and visual relevance and correctness) and the instability of LLM evaluation, we rely on human annotators to perform the classification.
guideline: Annotators determine correctness based on two criteria: Relevancy and Responsiveness.
determine the correctness of MLLMs' responses based on two criteria: Relevancy and Responsiveness

Annotators evaluated responses based on relevancy (whether the response is reflected in the image and addresses the question) and responsiveness (whether the response directly answers the question). They also classified answers by semantic closeness to reference responses in Vision or Knowledge categories.
